paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: when the LORD shows His servant something hard, the truth gets told. Elisha says Ben-hadad "will die" (2 Kings 8:10), and he doesn't water it down to match the happy answer. Hazael showed up with forty camel loads of gifts, and the answer was still the answer (2 Kings 8:9-10).

Now look at Elisha's tears. The man of God "began to weep" (2 Kings 8:11) because he knew the evil Hazael would do to the Israelites (2 Kings 8:12). I think that's the heart to copy, friend. Knowing a hard truth doesn't make us cold about it, and it should break our hearts for the people who will be hurt.

Then there's Hazael, who asks, "how could your servant, a mere dog, do such a monstrous thing?" (2 Kings 8:13). A few verses later he tells the sick king one thing, and the next day he does another (2 Kings 8:14-15). So don't ever say "I would NEVER" and then stop paying attention to your own heart. Stay close to the LORD and His Word, and stay honest in the small moments, friend.
